**Cross-workspace error code lost — demo shows `MUTATION_FAILED` instead of `DEMO_CROSS_WORKSPACE_DENIED`** `assertMutationSuccess` only inspects `result.errors` (an array) when building the thrown error. The cross-workspace denial response coming back from the server has the shape `{ ok: false, error: { code: "DEMO_CROSS_WORKSPACE_DENIED", … } }` — a single `error` object, not an `errors` array. Because `Array.isArray(result.errors)` is `false` here, `firstError` is always `null` and the thrown object gets `code: "MUTATION_FAILED"`. When `attemptCrossWorkspaceShare` catches that re-throw and calls `readErrorCode`, it receives `"MUTATION_FAILED"`, so the activity log and the `crossWorkspaceErrorCode` UI binding both show `MUTATION_FAILED` rather than the pedagogically important `DEMO_CROSS_WORKSPACE_DENIED`. The E2E test in `scope-and-isolation.spec.ts` passes only because it calls `runMutation` directly against the raw API, entirely bypassing this code path. To fix, also check the singular `.error.code` field: ```ts function assertMutationSuccess(result: unknown) { if ( typeof result === "object" && result !== null && "ok" in result && (result as { ok: unknown }).ok === false ) { const r = result as { errors?: unknown; error?: { code?: string; message?: string } }; const firstError = Array.isArray(r.errors) ? (r.errors as Array<{ code?: string; message?: string; path?: string }>)[0] ?? null : null; throw { code: firstError?.code ?? r.error?.code ?? "MUTATION_FAILED", message: firstError?.message ?? r.error?.message ?? "Mutation failed", details: { path: firstError?.path ?? "operation", }, }; } } ```

2\. Startup failures exit success 🐞 Bug ⛯ Reliability 
The todo-app server uses main().catch(console.error), which logs startup failures but does not set
a non-zero exit code. This can make scripts/CI treat a failed start as success and hide real startup
errors.
Agent Prompt ```` ### Issue description Startup errors are swallowed (logged only) and may exit with code 0. ### Issue Context This makes failures harder to detect in automation. ### Fix Focus Areas - datafn/examples/todo-app/server/src/index.ts[184-184] ### What to change Replace `main().catch(console.error);` with an error handler that sets a failure exit code, e.g.: ```ts main().catch((err) => { console.error(err); process.exitCode = 1; }); ``` (or `process.exit(1)` if you prefer immediate termination). ```` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate cross-workspace shares on all mutation endpoints**

The cross-workspace guard is only executed when the request path ends with `/mutation`, so equivalent share payloads sent through `/datafn/transact` (or sync `/datafn/push` mutations) bypass this check entirely and go straight to `datafn.router.handle`. That breaks the demo’s stated deterministic cross-workspace denial behavior for callers that use non-`/mutation` write paths.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reset rejected switch chain before queuing the next switch**

If one session switch fails, this promise chain stays rejected because the callback rethrows and there is no recovery handler; subsequent calls to `queueSessionSwitch` attach via `.then(...)` to an already rejected `switchChain`, so their switch logic never runs. In practice, a single transient clone/context error can permanently disable further workspace/user switching until a full page reload.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exit with failure code when server bootstrap throws**

Startup errors are swallowed by `main().catch(console.error)`, which logs the exception but leaves `process.exitCode` unset; Node then exits successfully even though initialization failed (for example, bad DB/search configuration). This makes CI/process managers misclassify failed boots as successful runs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
